chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the two of them, and he said: “They are part of wudu (ablution), so if you forget them, then do not repeat.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the authority being asked for the ruling
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification under discussion
key_terms.فَلَا تُعِدْ: do not repeat; an instruction that repetition is not required
key_terms.نَسِيتَهُمَا: you forgot the two of them; omission due to forgetfulness

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets part of wudu (ablution), must the wudu be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning two acts related to wudu (ablution), stating that they are part of the wudu. However, if they are omitted out of forgetfulness, the act does not need to be repeated. Its significance lies in distinguishing between what is included in the rite and what invalidates it when forgotten.
